abstract.text:
We propose kernel-based collocation methods for numerical solutions to Heath-
Jarrow-Morton models with Musiela parametrization. The methods can be seen as
the Euler-Maruyama approximation of some finite dimensional stochastic differential
equations, and allow us to compute the derivative prices by the usual Monte Carlo
methods. We derive a bound on the rate of convergence under some decay conditions on the interpolation functions and some regularity conditions on the volatility
functionals.

sections.summary: The paper introduces kernel-based collocation methods for numerical solutions to Heath-Jarrow-Merton models with Musiela parametrization. It frames the HJMM stochastic partial differential equation, positions the method as an alternative to finite element and splitting methods, and states the goal of deriving a convergence-rate bound under decay and regularity conditions.
sections.title: Introduction and contribution

sections.summary: Defines the Hilbert space U with a weighted Sobolev norm, the shift semigroup S(t), and states Proposition 2.1: separability, embedding into C_b^1, strong continuity, and generator A = φ'. This analytic framework underlies the HJMM well-posedness and convergence analysis.
sections.title: HJMM function space and semigroup

sections.summary: Proves Proposition 2.1. Separability is shown by embedding U into a product of auxiliary spaces, derivative bounds give U ⊂ C_b^1, and strong continuity of S(t) is reduced to a weighted L2 approximation argument. The generator is identified as Aφ = φ'.
sections.title: Semigroup proof and generator

sections.summary: Introduces measurable volatility mappings σ_i into U and Assumption 2.2: uniform boundedness and Lipschitz continuity. Defines the HJM drift α and proves Lemma 2.3, showing α is measurable, bounded, and Lipschitz in U, ensuring the drift term is well behaved.
sections.title: Volatility assumptions and α regularity

sections.summary: Uses the Da Prato-Zabczyk theorem to obtain a unique U-valued mild solution r(t) to the HJMM stochastic equation, with a uniform second-moment bound. Defines discounted bond prices and the forward rate f(t,T)=r(t,T−t), recovering HJM dynamics and linking the SPDE to risk-neutral interest-rate modeling.
sections.title: Well-posedness and financial interpretation

sections.summary: Reviews kernel-based interpolation using a radial positive definite function Φ, native space NΦ(R), and the interpolation operator I(g) on a finite set Γ. Adopts Wendland kernels Φτ, whose native space is equivalent to the Sobolev space H^{τ+1}.
sections.title: Kernel interpolation and Wendland kernels

sections.summary: Derives the finite-dimensional collocation approximation by replacing r and its derivative with interpolants. Collocation at Γ yields an N-dimensional SDE, and Euler-Maruyama time stepping produces the discrete process r^h. Evaluation at points Γe gives the practical algorithm.
sections.title: Collocation scheme and Euler-Maruyama discretization

sections.summary: States Assumption 3.1 on r0 and σ_i, and Assumption 3.2 on mesh parameters and cardinal functions Q_j. Remark 3.3 gives a quasi-uniform sufficient condition. Theorem 3.4 provides the main convergence rate bound for the collocation-Euler scheme.
sections.title: Convergence assumptions and main theorem

sections.summary: Presents stability and interpolation error lemmas. Lemma 3.5 bounds sums of cardinal-function derivatives. Lemma 3.6 gives interpolation error estimates in H^{τ+1} and C_b^{1+m}, using translation, extension, mollification, and optimization of a mollification parameter.
sections.title: Interpolation stability and error lemmas

sections.summary: Lemma 3.7 establishes a uniform second-moment bound for the Euler-Maruyama process r^h. The interpolated generator Ã = AI is shown bounded and generates a semigroup S̃. Lemma 3.8 bounds the semigroup approximation error on Γ ∪ Γe.
sections.title: Moment bounds and semigroup approximation

sections.summary: Proves Theorem 3.4 by representing r^h as a mild solution with remainder terms Θ, decomposing the squared error into I1–I6, bounding each term with Lemmas 3.5–3.8 and Assumption 3.1, and applying Gronwall’s lemma to obtain the claimed convergence rate.
sections.title: Proof of convergence theorem

sections.summary: Example 4.1 applies the collocation method to the Vasicek HJMM model. It gives the exact mild solution, parameter choices, Wendland kernel φ4, grid construction, numerical verification of Assumption 3.2, and RMSE results illustrating the convergence theorem.
sections.title: Vasicek numerical illustration

sections.summary: Example 4.2 prices caplets. It defines forward 6-month LIBOR, the caplet payoff, and a 5-year yield-dependent volatility model. It describes the grid parameters, Monte Carlo approximation, Assumption 3.2 checks, and plots of the approximated prices over θ1 and θ2.
sections.title: Caplet pricing numerical illustration

sections.summary: Optional navigation unit: bibliography listing 23 references on HJM models, stochastic PDEs, kernel methods, and numerical methods. It is not part of the substantive argument but provides source context for cited results.

sections.summary: The paper introduces kernel-based collocation methods for numerical solutions to Heath-Jarrow-Merton models with Musiela parametrization. It frames the HJMM stochastic partial differential equation, positions the method as an alternative to finite element and splitting methods, and states the goal of deriving a convergence-rate bound under decay and regularity conditions.
sections.title: Introduction and contribution

sections.summary: Defines the Hilbert space U with a weighted Sobolev norm, the shift semigroup S(t), and states Proposition 2.1: separability, embedding into C_b^1, strong continuity, and generator A = φ'. This analytic framework underlies the HJMM well-posedness and convergence analysis.
sections.title: HJMM function space and semigroup

sections.summary: Proves Proposition 2.1. Separability is shown by embedding U into a product of auxiliary spaces, derivative bounds give U ⊂ C_b^1, and strong continuity of S(t) is reduced to a weighted L2 approximation argument. The generator is identified as Aφ = φ'.
sections.title: Semigroup proof and generator

sections.summary: Introduces measurable volatility mappings σ_i into U and Assumption 2.2: uniform boundedness and Lipschitz continuity. Defines the HJM drift α and proves Lemma 2.3, showing α is measurable, bounded, and Lipschitz in U, ensuring the drift term is well behaved.
sections.title: Volatility assumptions and α regularity

sections.summary: Uses the Da Prato-Zabczyk theorem to obtain a unique U-valued mild solution r(t) to the HJMM stochastic equation, with a uniform second-moment bound. Defines discounted bond prices and the forward rate f(t,T)=r(t,T−t), recovering HJM dynamics and linking the SPDE to risk-neutral interest-rate modeling.
sections.title: Well-posedness and financial interpretation

sections.summary: Reviews kernel-based interpolation using a radial positive definite function Φ, native space NΦ(R), and the interpolation operator I(g) on a finite set Γ. Adopts Wendland kernels Φτ, whose native space is equivalent to the Sobolev space H^{τ+1}.
sections.title: Kernel interpolation and Wendland kernels

sections.summary: Derives the finite-dimensional collocation approximation by replacing r and its derivative with interpolants. Collocation at Γ yields an N-dimensional SDE, and Euler-Maruyama time stepping produces the discrete process r^h. Evaluation at points Γe gives the practical algorithm.
sections.title: Collocation scheme and Euler-Maruyama discretization

sections.summary: States Assumption 3.1 on r0 and σ_i, and Assumption 3.2 on mesh parameters and cardinal functions Q_j. Remark 3.3 gives a quasi-uniform sufficient condition. Theorem 3.4 provides the main convergence rate bound for the collocation-Euler scheme.
sections.title: Convergence assumptions and main theorem

sections.summary: Presents stability and interpolation error lemmas. Lemma 3.5 bounds sums of cardinal-function derivatives. Lemma 3.6 gives interpolation error estimates in H^{τ+1} and C_b^{1+m}, using translation, extension, mollification, and optimization of a mollification parameter.
sections.title: Interpolation stability and error lemmas

sections.summary: Lemma 3.7 establishes a uniform second-moment bound for the Euler-Maruyama process r^h. The interpolated generator Ã = AI is shown bounded and generates a semigroup S̃. Lemma 3.8 bounds the semigroup approximation error on Γ ∪ Γe.
sections.title: Moment bounds and semigroup approximation

sections.summary: Proves Theorem 3.4 by representing r^h as a mild solution with remainder terms Θ, decomposing the squared error into I1–I6, bounding each term with Lemmas 3.5–3.8 and Assumption 3.1, and applying Gronwall’s lemma to obtain the claimed convergence rate.
sections.title: Proof of convergence theorem

sections.summary: Example 4.1 applies the collocation method to the Vasicek HJMM model. It gives the exact mild solution, parameter choices, Wendland kernel φ4, grid construction, numerical verification of Assumption 3.2, and RMSE results illustrating the convergence theorem.
sections.title: Vasicek numerical illustration

sections.summary: Example 4.2 prices caplets. It defines forward 6-month LIBOR, the caplet payoff, and a 5-year yield-dependent volatility model. It describes the grid parameters, Monte Carlo approximation, Assumption 3.2 checks, and plots of the approximated prices over θ1 and θ2.
sections.title: Caplet pricing numerical illustration

sections.summary: Optional navigation unit: bibliography listing 23 references on HJM models, stochastic PDEs, kernel methods, and numerical methods. It is not part of the substantive argument but provides source context for cited results.
sections.title: References

type.reason: This paper proposes kernel-based collocation methods for HJMM models and analyzes their convergence with numerical experiments.
